All done. Both platforms build clean and the logic is verified. Here's the summary.

## What I built

**Background batch AI word-analysis** — a new engine + UI that analyzes all your saved vocabulary with the current AI model, in parallel, persisting results.

**New engine** — `Models/BatchExplanationController.swift`: an `@Observable @MainActor` singleton (matching every other store). It owns the background `Task` and a `withTaskGroup` sliding window, so:
- It only analyzes words with **no cached explanation** for the current direction (the same cache the detail view reads).
- Results persist via the existing `WordExplanationCacheStore` (keyed by `headlineText` + direction, so the detail view serves them instantly).
- Because it's a singleton, **navigating away — even closing Settings — doesn't stop it**, and any view observing it shows live progress.

**Settings UI** — `Views/Components/BatchAIAnalysisView.swift`:
- **Batch-size stepper** (1–10 parallel words, persisted in `AIModelSettings.batchConcurrency`).
- **"Analyze N Words"** button (only counts unanalyzed words; disabled when none/no provider).
- Once running: a **progress bar**, a **live "✓ done / total" count**, the last analyzed word, and a **Cancel** button.
- Reachable from **iOS More → Batch AI Analysis** (with a live progress badge on the row itself) and embedded in **macOS Settings → AI**.

**Per-word rerun** — the detail view's analysis header now has a clear labeled **"Regenerate"** button that re-runs with the current model.

**Import/export** — AI analysis now round-trips in both formats (toggle in both export UIs): JSON via a versioned envelope (lossless), CSV via human-readable `AI Definition`/`AI Examples` columns plus a base64 `AI Data` column. Both are backward-compatible with old files.

## Edges I ironed out
I ran a 92-agent adversarial audit (51 confirmed issues) in parallel. It caught a **compile bug in my own code** before the first build (uninitialized `batchConcurrency`). I fixed that plus the feature-relevant ones: stale AI-analysis state when reusing the view for a different word, mislabeled provider on cached results, and a CSV multi-line-quoted-field round-trip bug. A standalone Swift test then caught a **second real bug** — Swift treats `\r\n` as one grapheme, so my CSV splitter ignored Windows/Excel line endings; fixed with `Character.isNewline`. Pre-existing, out-of-scope findings are documented in `docs/handoff/batch-ai-analysis/handoff.md` for a follow-up.

## What the SIGTERM was

`SIGTERM` isn't a memory crash — it's a termination signal, and the debugger parking on `normalizedKey` was the tell: the **main thread was spinning there**. My batch UI caused it. `BatchAIAnalysisControls` recomputed the "unprocessed words" count **on every render and ~4× per render** (for `analyzed`, "Needs Analysis", the button label, and `.disabled`), and each computation scanned the *entire* explanation cache calling `normalizedKey()` per entry — **O(terms × entries)** with a string allocation each time. Since the view re-renders on every cache store and every progress tick during a batch, the main thread saturated → watchdog termination.

## The fixes (commit `c827d8b`, pushed)
1. **O(1) cache lookup** — `WordExplanationCacheStore` now maintains a `lookupIndex` set (kept in sync via `entries.didSet`); `hasExplanation()` is a set membership test instead of a full O(n) scan. The index is observed, so the live count still updates.
2. **Compute once per render** — `BatchAIAnalysisControls` computes the unprocessed count a single time in `body` and threads it down, instead of recomputing it in each subview.

Together these turn the per-render cost from O(terms × entries) into O(terms) with no inner string churn — the hot path that was burning the main thread is gone.

## Also fixed: project-file warnings
While verifying, a separate issue surfaced: **a local hook had mangled `project.pbxproj`**, injecting triplicated `PBXBuildFile`/`Sources` entries for my new files (and references to `logs/`/session JSON). Since the project uses a synchronized root group that auto-compiles everything, those explicit entries double-counted files → "duplicate build file" warnings. My committed `pbxproj` (HEAD) was already clean; I discarded the working-tree junk and confirmed the build returns to **0 warnings**, and the pbxproj stayed clean across a rebuild.

⚠️ Heads-up: that hook re-adds stray `.pbxproj` references on tool activity (it's why the file showed as modified at session start). It didn't re-trigger this time, but if you see `project.pbxproj` go dirty with duplicate build-file entries again, `git checkout HEAD -- SwiftMandarin.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj` restores the clean synchronized-group form.

Verified: clean macOS build, 0 errors / 0 warnings. If the SIGTERM recurs in a different scenario (e.g. a specific Preview, or at launch), send the full Xcode console / crash context and I'll dig further — but the batch-run hang is resolved.
